newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ireland's Quinn sees eight nations at Euro start.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Quinn sees eight nations at Euro start.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said on Friday he believed eight countries could participate in the start of European monetary union in 1999.

Quinn told a conference three countries -- Denmark, Luxembourg and Ireland -- appeared to have already fulfilled the criteria for joining the proposed single currency as outlined in the Maastricht Treaty.
European Union Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy, speaking at the same conference, said he believed at least three countries would be ready for the start of a single currency.

Under terms of the treaty, European countries wanting to join monetary union must meet strict criteria on debts and deficits, inflation, long-term interest rates and currency stability by the end of 1997.
